{{Quote|Equipped with a variety of useful features, the droid is a valuable part of the laboratory environment.|Toria Tell's Droid Journal|<ref name="Toria" />}}
The '''Science Research Droid'''&mdash;designated the '''S2R droid''' by the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]]&mdash;was a [[biological science droid]] constructed by [[TelBrinTel Corporation]] for use in the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] chemical and [[Bioweapon/Legends|biological weapon]] projects, as well as [[Armor/Legends|armor]] and power-guidance system development. It was a vaguely [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] unit measuring 1.9 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in height, with two fine-control manipulator [[Limb/Legends|arms]] and two legs possessing a suspension system that cushioned its steps. It was built with an advanced [[protocol chip]] for communicating with organic [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]], a molecular [[Microscope/Legends|microscope]] and sophisticated [[Olfactory sensor/Legends|olfactory analysis]] technology, and an "[[endosystem]]" designed to mount accessories on six ports located in its upper torso. The droid's success in the Imperial Military led TelBrinTel to create the civilian [[S2R(A) Science Droid|S2R(A)]] model, designed to match the original droid's performance but with security features preventing it from working on weapons or military projects.

==Description==
The Science Research [[Droid/Legends|Droid]] was a [[Class one droid/Legends|class one droid]]<ref name="Cynabar" /> of the [[Biological science droid|biological science class]]<ref name="Bio" /> measuring 1.9 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall and having a vaguely [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] appearance. It possessed a highly advanced [[protocol chip]] in its [[Droid brain/Legends|droid brain]],<ref name="Toria" /> enabling it to engage in "creative brainstorming" sessions with living [[Scientist/Legends|coworkers]].<ref name="Cynabar" /> Its monocular [[Eye/Legends|eyepiece]]<ref name="Toria" /> contained a high-powered, multi-spectrum molecular microscope,<ref name="Cynabar" /> and it possessed [[Olfactory sensor/Legends|olfactory sensors]] and a sophisticated olfactory databank<ref name="Toria" /> and analysis package.<ref name="Cynabar" /> Its two [[Limb/Legends|arms]] were designed for fine control and manipulation, and its two legs were equipped with a suspension system that cushioned each step,<ref name="Toria" /> preventing unstable chemicals and compounds from potentially dangerous jarring.<ref name="Cynabar" /> The droid's upper torso held its "[[endosystem]]," a marketable feature that provided six ports on the droid's vertebrae for the attachment of dockable accessories. These accessories could include additional arms, work surfaces, or small tools or injection needles.<ref name="Toria" />

==History==
The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] commissioned the Science Research Droid from [[TelBrinTel Corporation]]<ref name="Toria" /> for use in the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military's]] chemical and [[Bioweapon/Legends|biological weapon]] programs, and also for research into new [[Armor/Legends|armor]] and power-guidance systems for the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]]. The droid, designated the "S2R droid" by the military,<ref name="Cynabar" /> first reached Imperial research centers in large numbers immediately after the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]]<ref name="Toria" /> in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> A large portion of this initial shipment wound up in the hands of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]].<ref name="Toria" /> Despite this, the droid's performance in the Imperial Military was regarded as a marked success, leading to production of a civilian-oriented model. This model, the [[S2R(A) Science Droid|S2R(A)]], performed many of the same functions as the initial model, though hardwired protocols prevented the droids from knowingly working on weaponry or projects with military applications. These protocols could be bypassed, but secret programming installed by TelBrinTel would then kick in, causing the modified droid to modify chemical formulas so that the resultant products were inert.<ref name="Cynabar" />

The original Science Research Droid caught the attention of [[Toria Tell]], a droid inventor and collector who maintained "[[Toria Tell's Droid Journal (scandoc)|Toria Tell's Droid Journal]]," a small, private [[Scandoc/Legends|scandoc]] distributed in a limited fashion around [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="Toria" /> The droid was also featured in Version 4.7.110 of [[Cynabar's Droid Datalog]], which discussed both the S2R and S2R(A) models. There, Tell added commentary to the droid's entry, informing readers of the surreptitious programming added by TelBrinTel to thwart those who bypass the hardwired protocols of the S2R(A). Another reader, a [[Slicer/Legends|slicer]] using the pseudonym "[[Ranger (slicer)|Ranger]]," confirmed Tell's information. Ranger had been hired by Rebels to remove such safeguards in similar droids, and noted that the TelBrinTel subroutines were quite subtle, hard to locate, and deeply ingrained in the droid's systems.<ref name="Cynabar" />

Numerous TelBrinTel science droids were used by the [[Baobab Archives]], which assigned many of them to analyze the ''[[Dha Werda Verda]]'', an ancient poem etched into [[Roonstone]]s discovered by the [[Merchant/Legends|merchant]] [[Mungo Baobab]].<ref name="Golden Droid">''[[C-3PO: Tales of the Golden Droid]]''</ref>

One notable Science Research Droid was [[Geth]]. This droid had been modified by former Rebel [[General/Legends|General]] [[Reesen Jivrak]], who had been ejected from the Rebel Alliance for his unethical and cruel conduct. He used Geth to create [[Poison/Legends|toxins]] that would strengthen and enrage the docile [[deripor]]s of [[Ohratuu]] for use as mounts in hit-and-run attacks.<ref name="Toria" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Science Research Droid was introduced in [[Toria Tell's Droid Journal (article)|''Toria Tell's Droid Journal'']], an article written and illustrated by [[Christian Piccolo]], published in [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 10|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 10]] in May [[1996]].<ref name="Toria" />
